newsitem.title: USA: FIGURE SKATING-KWAN, ELDREDGE WIN SKATE AMERICA TITLES.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-KWAN, ELDREDGE WIN SKATE AMERICA TITLES.

text.p: World figure skating champions Michelle Kwan and Todd Eldredge of the United States won individual titles on Saturday at Skate America International, the first major international event of the season.
Both the 16-year-old Kwan and Eldredge, 25, had led after the short programme and stayed in first place after Saturday's free-skating routines.

In pairs, the Russian team of Oksana Kazakova and Artur Dmitriev moved up from second place in the free-skating programme and captured the title from Americans Shelby Lyons and Brian Wells, who had led after the short programme but finished second.
Anjelika Krylova and Oleg Ovsiannikov of Russia won the ice dancing championship with another Russian team, Irina Lobatcheva and Ilia Averbukh, in second place.
Third place went to the French team of Sophie Moniotte and Pascal Lavanchy, who were returning to competition after missing more than a year to injury problems.
Skate America opened the six-event Champions Series, which next moves to the Canadian venue of Kitchener, Ontario, where competition begins Thursday.
Kwan felt she needed to improve her conditioning.
"It could have been better, but I am very happy," said Kwan. "I was pretty comfortable, but we have work to do."
American women finished 1-2-3 with Tonia Kwiatkowski second and Sydne Vogel third.
Eldredge showed an advanced programme for such an early-season event. He received 5.9's from all but one of the nine judges.

"I think everything could be a bit more polished, but I'm very happy," he said to suggestions that his routine was approaching perfection. He held on to first place despite a strong bid by Russian Alexei Urmanov to unseat him.
Asked what it would take to defeat Eldredge if the American's current level continued, Urmanov smiled and said: "Very difficult question -- maybe some more difficult combinations, I don't know."
In pairs, the Kazakova-Dmitriev team looked much better than they had in Thursday's short programme.

"We've worked much more on the free programme than the short programme, and when you're more comfortable, you can give more energy," Dmitriev said. "We are happy for the Americans (Lyons and Wells), though. We practiced with them in Colorado Springs, Colorado, and they've progressed greatly."
The Krylova-Ovsiannikov ice dancing champions attributed their success to hard work in the offseason, though Krylova joked that she worked harder than her partner.
"I did cross country running," she said. "Oleg, he just sleeps and eats red meat."
